newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta gathers strength despite B/Spain rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Peseta gathers strength despite B/Spain rate cut.

text.p: The peseta strengthened against the mark on Friday, capitalising on the strength of the domestic economy and shrugging aside a Bank of Spain rate cut.
"After several days of light pressure, the market has turned optimistic thanks to the good economic state and it has resumed peseta purchases," a dealer said.

The dealer said that after the quarter-point cut today the Bank of Spain had reserved scope for another decline in June, which would serve in coming weeks to underpin bonds and shares and therefore the peseta.
Earlier, the Bank of Spain cut its key money market rate to 5.25 prcent from 5.50 percent in a widely expected move.
At 1030 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.28/30 per mark after opening at 84.34/36 and closing Wednesday at 84.41/42.
The pullback of the mark in other European crosses was also supporting the peseta.
